title: Choose the look for Ithaca's App Store screenshots
question: The roll assigned Festival Programme. Keep it, take my pick or an alternate, or re-roll. Expand a card to see its first iPhone slide full size. Sketches use Blender's open movies (CC BY); the final slides use real captures from the app.

options.label: Festival Programme
options.lineage: Film festival programme books (Cannes, TIFF, NYFF catalogues)
options.thesis: Each slide is a programme entry: your library billed like a festival screening, with its format line.
options.viewport: A coral section band, the headline set as a film title across the full width, a credits block with the format line, the iPhone below as the entry's still, screening times along the foot.
options.risk: Festival paper can read bookish; it holds only while the device is big and the type heavy.

raised.raise: The device screen is the only full-colour thing on a slide; everything else stays two-colour print.
The six slides run as one evening's programme, screening times stepping from 7 PM to the late show.
Each slide's foot prints the next entry's title, so the set reads in order.
One type family at its extremes: titles at full width, credits at caption size, nothing between.

options.label: Back of the Box
options.lineage: 4K disc keepcases and their back-cover spec panels
options.thesis: Each slide is the back of a 4K disc case: a big still, a short pitch, and the spec panel collectors read first.
options.viewport: Black case band with the name set as a title treatment, the iPhone over a full-bleed still, a ruled spec grid (video, audio, subtitles) at the foot.
options.risk: Familiar: most home-theater marketing lands here; spec text reads technical and no Dolby or disc logos may appear.

options.label: The Select Rail
options.lineage: A film editor's cutting bench: work print on pins, tape flags
options.thesis: Your library strung as frames on a perforated rail, a tape flag folded at the frame where you stopped.
options.viewport: Coral grain field, the rail crossing at a fixed height with poster frames, the flag on the resumed film, the iPhone in a punched white window below.
options.case: Film lovers read a strip at once and the flag is Continue Watching; loses on native Apple feel.
options.risk: Production-tool imagery can read as an editing app.

options.label: The Readout
options.lineage: Viewfinder brackets and AV receiver front-panel readouts
options.thesis: A full-bleed film still, brackets closing on the device, and the format readouts in the corners.
options.viewport: Letterboxed still edge to edge, brackets around the iPhone, corner readouts (2160p, DV, ATMOS, DIRECT) and a resume counter, headline under the top bar.
options.case: The readouts are the direct-play claim; camcorder chrome is consumer video, not home theater.
options.risk: Readout type at thumbnail size can turn to noise.

options.label: Akari Lanterns
options.thesis: Slides as glowing paper volumes in a dim room.
options.viewport: A lantern glow around the device.
options.case: Paper lanterns say neither Plex nor home theater.
options.kept: One light source: the screen is the only lit thing.

options.label: Rain-Night City
options.thesis: The set as a city's evening, hour by hour.
options.case: Mood without the product; says nothing about your library or direct play.
options.kept: The six slides run as one evening.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: The library as a code buffer on a projector.
options.case: Plex owners watching films don't identify with live coding.
options.kept: What's next is visible before it plays.

options.label: Merz Collage
options.thesis: Tickets and torn type glued around the device.
options.case: Fights the native, quiet app it sells.
options.kept: Type at its extremes from one case.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark gradient, a bold centred headline, the device below: what most players ship, done cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and one line on a dark gradient, the iPhone centred below.
canonCard.risk: It is the look of Dusk for Plex's own listing, the app Ithaca descends from.
